projects.name: 1.1.2.13 - Reversing land degradation trands and increasing food security in degraded ecosystems of semi-arid areas of Tanzania
projects.description:
Project development objective is to reverse land degradation trends through sustainable land and water management and ecosystems based adaptation. The LDFS is structured into three inter-related components: Component 1 will set the enabling conditions for sustainable land and water management at landscape level sustaining ecosystem services and enhancing food security. It will strengthen institutional capacity at the village, inter-village and district levels and establish inter-village committees with the goal of developing landscape level inter-village participatory resources and livelihood diagnostics and land use planning processes to foster an integrated and holistic management of natural resources. Component 2 will support the implementation of sustainable land and water management priorities, conservation of habitats for biodiversity, conservation farming practices, and income-generating activities agreed within said plans. Component 3 will focus on monitoring and assessing the progress in sustaining ecosystem services, household resilience and food security based on assessment results. Component 3 will also support incorporating lessons learned in local and district level natural resources governance systems and contributing to the continuous improvement of the landscape level approach to natural resources management, supporting integration of best practices in policy making at the district, regional and national levels.

Budgeting is done on annual basis at national level.  At the start of the fiscal year, beneficiaries districts (Kondoa, Magu, Micheweni, Mkalama, Nzega) submit their annual work plan and budget and the coordination unit transfer the funds to each district according to their needs.

projects.name: 1.1.3.51 - Innovation and ecosystem strengthening activities
projects.description: WFP believes that innovation is crucial to improving the lives of those furthest behind. Bold, creative innovations in technology, nutrition and agriculture have the potential to create extraordinary, life-changing impact for millions of people.  To this end, WFP’s first Field Innovation Hub (the Hub) was established in Tanzania in 2017. The Hub complements the global WFP Innovation Accelerator (the Accelerator). Now in its third year, the Hub has laid the groundwork for catalysing Tanzania’s innovation ecosystem and changing the way WFP approaches both current and future operations. The Hub’s work in Tanzania focuses on four areas: 1) catalysing the Tanzania Innovation ecosystem; 2) designing and implementing innovation pilots with SDG2-focused startups; 3) providing innovation services to WFP operations in Tanzania 4) building partnerships

projects.name: 1.1.3.45 - Support to Host Communities with focus on Food and Economic Security through Agriculture
projects.description: In order to align with Government priorities around the Agricultural Sector Development Plan II (ASDP 2) and other current interventions in the Kigoma region, the Kigoma Joint Programme Agriculture theme (Outcome 6) adopts the partnership approach to address issues pertaining to smallholders farmers. FAO interventions under the programme, focus on improving agricultural productivity through promoting Climate Smart Agriculture, creating access to knowledge on Good Agricultural Practices, access to high quality inputs that are adapted to local conditions such as climate conditions and pest and disease pressure, to increase the productivity of identified crops (Maize, Cassava and Beans). FAO continues to play a critical role in providing technical support through advocating for the implementation of the Tanzania Agriculture and Climate Resilience Plan (ACRP) and Climate Smart Agriculture Programme to mitigate risks, set priorities for action and investment and build a foundation for resilience in the agriculture sector especially for vulnerable communities. This reiterates the government’s commitment to make the agricultural sector climate-smart by 2030. A comprehensive training package on Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) emphasizing on Climate Smart Agriculture (CSA) for crop production will entail on/off farm practices that address environmental, economic and social sustainability aspects along the supply chain, which results to safe and quality food and non-food products. This will enable farmers to become resilient to climate shock. Emphasis will also be placed on nutrition-sensitive agriculture to address the double burden of malnutrition in the region.The CSA guideline will be used as an instructive tool for informing extension staff and farmers on mainstreaming climate change adaptation and mitigation co-beneficial objectives within agriculture development. More particularly, it will provide guidance on CSA practices and technologies best suited for Kigoma region and the agro-climatic zone. It will also target district development planners and extension agents to plan and budget for agricultural development, and to facilitate community level planning; and extension agents to sensitize, mobilize and train smallholder farmers to adopt agricultural practices considered climate-smart. Additionally, FAO will train smallholder farmers on improved beekeeping practices as an important livelihood strategy for income generating with very high potential for improving income, especially for communities living close to forests and woodlands. - Establish and implement a functional multi-sectoral dialogue and coordination mechanism at national and subnational levels . This will result in greater efficiency and effectiveness of social protection in reaching the poor & vulnerable by increasing coherence of policies, idenfying gaps, avoiding duplications, maximising synergies across sectors towards the establishment of a comprehensive & integrated system. Sensitisation on social protection at all government levels will also be supported.

- Support the development and operationalisation of costed implementation plans for the NSPP and ZSPP, with a focus on increasing and improving public spending on social protection, via conducting public expenditure reviews, costing exercises, and identification of fiscal space options. The goal is to ensure that plans are executed with greater national financing and thereby increased sustainability. 

- Build a social protection monitoring, evaluation and knowledge management system at national and sub-national levels. The goal is to measure progress towards the objectives set in NSPP and ZSPP, as well as poverty-related priorities in key national plans, particularly the Five Year Development Plan II and the Mkuza Successor Strategy.

projects.name: 4.2.2.2 - Support to Host Communities with focus on Food and Economic Security through Agriculture
projects.description:
In order to align with Government priorities around the Agricultural Sector Development Plan II (ASDP 2) and other current interventions in the Kigoma region, the Kigoma Joint Programme Agriculture theme (Outcome 6) adopts the partnership approach to address issues pertaining to smallholders farmers. 

FAO interventions under the programme,  focus on improving agricultural productivity through promoting Climate Smart Agriculture, creating access to knowledge on Good Agricultural Practices, access to high quality inputs that are adapted to local conditions such as climate conditions and pest and disease pressure, to increase the productivity of identified crops (Maize, Cassava and Beans).

FAO continues to play a critical role in providing technical support through advocating for the implementation of the Tanzania Agriculture and Climate Resilience Plan (ACRP) and Climate Smart Agriculture Programme to mitigate risks, set priorities for action and investment and build a foundation for resilience in the agriculture sector especially for vulnerable communities. This reiterates the government’s commitment to make the agricultural sector climate-smart by 2030. 

A comprehensive training package on Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) emphasizing on Climate Smart Agriculture (CSA) for crop production will entail on/off farm practices that address environmental, economic and social sustainability aspects along the supply chain, which results to safe and quality food and non-food products. This will enable farmers to become resilient to climate shock. Emphasis will also be placed on nutrition-sensitive agriculture to address the double burden of malnutrition in the region.

The CSA guideline will be used as an instructive tool for informing extension staff and farmers on mainstreaming climate change adaptation and mitigation co-beneficial objectives within agriculture development. More particularly, it will provide guidance on CSA practices and technologies best suited for Kigoma region and the agro-climatic zone. It will also target district development planners and extension agents to plan and budget for agricultural development, and to facilitate community level planning; and extension agents to sensitize, mobilize and train smallholder farmers to adopt agricultural practices considered climate-smart. 

Additionally, FAO will train smallholder farmers on improved beekeeping practices as an important livelihood strategy for income generating with very high potential for improving income, especially for communities living close to forests and woodlands.  Beekeeping development also has a potential of contributing to self-employment, enhancing agricultural production, promoting and the conservation of the environment.

FAO interventions will focus on the following outputs for the next four years: 
- Strengthening group cohesion and building producer organizations through Farmer Field Schools (FFS) and Junior Farmer Field Learning Schools (JFFLS)
- Training on good agriculture practices and Climate Smart Agriculture practices for selected commodities including maize, beans, cassava and livestock production
- Procurement and distribution of agricultural inputs (seeds and fertilizer, herbicides/pesticides, vaccines) and tools.
- Disseminate information about different and appropriate varieties of maize, beans and cassava and livestock through various channels including community radios, school JFFLS and FFS programmes.
- Promote and train Beekeeping as a viable enterprise (incl. dissemination of information via community radio)
- Develop and implement integrated landscape management plans in the project area/ agricultural zone

projects.name: 3.1.2.29 - Support Persons with Disabilities to reach their goals in accordance with international standards
projects.description:
This project focuses in supporting persons with disabilities (PWDs) to reach their goals, especially in terms of employment rights. The project will support for protection of the rights of PWDs as enshrined in the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, 2006 (CRPD) and in the relevant ILO Standards [Convention on Vocational Rehabilitation and Employment of Disabled Persons, 1983 (No. 159), Human Resources Development Recommendation, 2004 (No. 195) and the ILO Code of Practice on Managing Disability in the Workplace of 2001]. The provisions of these international instruments would benefit PWDs whose inability to find jobs due to social exclusion affect their lives both economically and socially. The CRPD and ILO Standards prohibit discrimination on the basis of disability in all forms of employment, and call on states to open up opportunities in mainstream workplaces to job seekers with disabilities. 

This project will, thus, focus on supporting PWDs to access the labour market, protecting rights of PWDs against all forms of discrimination at work place, and support disabled people find and keep jobs by promoting improved accessibility of workplaces. The project will also support PWDs to participate in national dialogue fora relating to their rights. The ILO will work with governments, employers' and workers' organizations as well as disabled persons' organizations in the United Republic of Tanzania to implement the project.

projects.name: 2.1.1.17 - Support the updating of the National Malaria Diagnosis and Treatment Guidelines
projects.description: The National Guidelines for Malaria Diagnosis and Treatment (NGMDT) serve as a reference to diverse health profession cadres in all levels of health care delivery in Tanzania. The gudielines provide a framework for development of different field manuals for malaria diagnosis and treatment and related pharmaceutical supplies protocols. The broad objective of these guidelines is to provide standard management reference for the care of patients with malaria at different levels of health care in both the public and private sector. The last publication was in 2014 and since then a number of interventions related to case management have been introduced or in the process of being established including iCCM, case based surveillance, routine testing all pregnant women at the first ANC and Malaria Service Delivery Quality Initiative (MSDQI). This calls for the need to update the current NGMDT in collaboration with AFRO, WHO/HQ and other malaria stakeholders.
projects.outcome: Output 2.1.1 - Relevant MDAs and select LGAs are better able to formulate and monitor implementation of evidence-based, equitable health policies, strategies and guidelines
